dedupe_keys.name: autoplan automatic cellular network planning with a digital radio twin and bayesian optimisation

description: AutoPlan is a framework for automatic cellular network planning that builds a digital radio twin (DRT) by fine-tuning the parameters of building materials from crowdsourced real-world user data, which reduces the gap between simulation and reality. A Bayesian optimisation algorithm then selects base station deployment parameters that maximise coverage and capacity. Evaluated with field measurements from Husker-Net under several deployment scenarios, it achieves performance comparable to exhaustive search while needing less than 2 percent of its computation time. Producer: Xiaomeng Li and seven co-authors; first posted 15 September 2025, revised to version 3 on 23 February 2026 (accepted at IEEE ICC 2026). Coverage: the Husker-Net test network. Access: paper on arXiv; no code or data link was read on the abstract page. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: results come from one field network and only the abstract page was read. Simulation uses: the twin and optimiser support coverage and capacity planning of mobile base stations. Related records: none linked.
